run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The failing workload is Deployment cart in namespace astronomy-shop. Its pod cart-74587775fc-dxrtf is in CrashLoopBackOff (restartCount 4 at 15:47:51Z, each termination exitCode 139 reason Error) and the cart container's log shows 'Unhandled exception. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' thrown from cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected()/Initialize() at startup. Because the cart container never becomes ready, the cart Service has only a notReadyAddresses entry, and callers get connection refused on 10.96.163.124:8080: frontend spans record HTTP 500 on GET/POST /api/cart and POST /api/checkout, checkout spans record gRPC 13/14 'cart failure ... connection refused', and the load generator's only failing endpoint is GET /api/cart (fail ratio 0.25 on 4 requests). The dependency valkey-cart was checked and looks healthy (Ready, 0 restarts, 'Ready to accept connections tcp', 3.4 MB of a 64 MiB limit, ready endpoint), and the crashing pod's own wait-for-valkey-cart init container reached valkey-cart (10.96.103.133:6379) two seconds before the cart app failed to connect, so valkey-cart is not shown to be the faulty object. Two things remain unresolved and make this partial: why the app's Redis connection fails while the init container reached the same address, and what replaced the cart pod at 15:44:46Z although the Deployment template stayed at revision 1. The whole namespace was (re)created at 15:43:47Z, so there is no pre-incident baseline.

claims.text: Deployment cart has no ready or available replicas (status.readyReplicas and status.availableReplicas null, updatedReplicas 1), while each of the other 22 deployments in astronomy-shop reports ready=1 and available=1 for 1 desired replica.

Pod cart-74587775fc-dxrtf (owner ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc, node sregym-worker3) has container cart not ready with restartCount 4 and state waiting/CrashLoopBackOff; its last termination was exitCode 139, reason Error, startedAt 2026-11-21T15:46:21Z, finishedAt 2026-11-21T15:46:27Z (observed 15:47:51Z).

An earlier snapshot at 15:45:22Z of the same pod already showed restartCount 2 with lastState.terminated exitCode 139 reason Error finishedAt 2026-11-21T15:45:09Z, and pod conditions Ready=False/ContainersReady=False with reason ContainersNotReady and message 'containers with unready status: [cart]'.

The cart container's restart-instance log (pod cart-74587775fc-dxrtf, file cart/1.log) contains at 15:44:50.268Z: 'Unhandled exception. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' with stack frames cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected() (ValkeyCartStore.cs:101) -> cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.Initialize() (ValkeyCartStore.cs:71) -> Program.<Main>$ (Program.cs:98/45).

The Endpoints object cart contains only a notReadyAddresses entry (10.244.125.40, targetRef pod cart-74587775fc-dxrtf) and no ready address, whereas Endpoints valkey-cart lists a ready address 10.244.7.244:6379 (targetRef pod valkey-cart-859985f49d-fp4l2).

Frontend spans between 15:44:59Z and 15:45:07Z record HTTP 500 on GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart and POST /api/checkout, and gRPC status 13/14 with message '...dial tcp 10.96.163.124:8080: connect: connection refused' on oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder; checkout, frontend-proxy and load-generator spans in the same traces carry HTTP 500 / error status.

At 15:45:00Z the load generator reported locust_requests_fail_ratio 0.25 with 4 aggregated requests and 1 aggregated failure, and the only per-endpoint failure series was method=GET name=/api/cart (1 failure of 1 request); every other per-endpoint failure counter was 0.

The cart pod's init container wait-for-valkey-cart logged 'valkey-cart (10.96.103.133:6379) open' at 2026-11-21T15:44:47.673Z, i.e. TCP connectivity from the cart pod's network namespace to the valkey-cart ClusterIP succeeded about 2.5 s before the cart container's 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' exception at 15:44:50.268Z.

valkey-cart was running and ready with 0 restarts since 15:43:49Z, logged 'Ready to accept connections tcp' at 15:43:52Z, had a container working set of 3,391,488 bytes against a 67,108,864-byte memory limit, and its Deployment valkey-cart reports 1/1 ready.

Deployment cart carries annotation deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=1; its ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc created pod cart-74587775fc-t6vdk at 15:43:47Z and pod cart-74587775fc-dxrtf at 15:44:46Z after the t6vdk container was stopped ('Stopping container cart', reason Killing, 15:44:46Z), and the only Deployment event returned for cart is 'Scaled up replica set cart-74587775fc from 0 to 1' at 15:43:47Z.

Before it was stopped, the previous cart container (pod cart-74587775fc-t6vdk) served ValkeyCartStore GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync/EmptyCartAsync calls up to 15:44:45.8Z and logged a graceful 'Application is shutting down...' at 15:44:46.44Z; its container memory working set was 41,095,168 bytes against the cart container's 167,772,160-byte limit.
container_oom_events_total is 0 at 15:45:00Z for every astronomy-shop container, including container cart on pod cart-74587775fc-t6vdk.

ConfigMap flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) declares cart-related fault flags cartFailure ('Fail cart service') and failedReadinessProbe ('readiness probe failure for cart service') both with state ENABLED but defaultVariant 'off', and no flag in that ConfigMap has a defaultVariant other than 'off'.

The otel-collector-agent DaemonSet pods otel-collector-agent-z554j, -psgfg and -5gdl6 were stopped between 15:44:31Z and 15:44:38Z and replaced by otel-collector-agent-g6rr8, -tgb8s and -zcbdf, seen as DaemonSet SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete events and 'Stopping container opentelemetry-collector' events; this is a collector DaemonSet replacement during install, not a cart event.

Most likely mechanism: the cart application cannot establish its Valkey/Redis connection while constructing ValkeyCartStore at startup (Program.cs registers the store lazily, EnsureRedisConnected/Initialize then throws System.ApplicationException 'Wasn't able to connect to redis'), the unhandled exception terminates the process (exit code 139), the container never becomes ready, and every caller of the cart Service therefore gets connection refused.

Unresolved alternative for the same crash: something specific to the cart pod's own egress/configuration changed between the successful init-container check at 15:44:47Z and the app's connect attempt at ~15:44:49Z (for example an unreadable Calico CRD-based policy, or a Redis address/setting the app uses that differs from the init container's valkey-cart:6379); the available evidence cannot distinguish this from a pure application-startup defect.

valkey-cart is not supported as the failing component: it was Ready with 0 restarts, logged 'Ready to accept connections tcp', had a ready endpoint 10.244.7.244:6379, used 3.4 MB of a 64 MiB limit, and the affected pod's own init container connected to valkey-cart:6379 successfully at 15:44:47Z.

Cart memory exhaustion/OOM at the 160Mi limit as the reason for exit code 139 is not supported: container_oom_events_total stayed 0, the previous cart container ran with the same 167,772,160-byte limit at ~41 MB working set and served requests normally, and the termination reason reported for the crashes is 'Error', not OOMKilled.

An enabled flagd fault flag is not supported as the trigger: the flagd-config ConfigMap delivered shows cartFailure and failedReadinessProbe with defaultVariant 'off' (and every other flag off), and the observed failure is an unhandled Redis-connection exception in the cart process, not a flag-driven error response or readiness-probe rejection; the live in-memory flag state served by flagd could not be read with the available tools.

Human follow-up: read the current and previous cart container logs on pod cart-74587775fc-dxrtf (the instances after 15:45:08Z are outside this run's window) and check the cart Deployment's pod template against the reference chart, in particular VALKEY_ADDR/ASPNETCORE_URLS and the wait-for-valkey-cart init container, which verifies a different target than the app apparently uses.

Human follow-up: identify the actor that deleted pod cart-74587775fc-t6vdk at 15:44:46Z (Deployment revision stayed 1, no eviction or OOMKilled event was returned) and check Calico CRD-based policies (GlobalNetworkPolicy/NetworkPolicy in crd.projectcalico.org) and the live flagd flag state, none of which are readable through the tools available in this run.

gaps: The reason the cart application's Valkey/Redis connection fails is unknown: its own init container reached valkey-cart (10.96.103.133:6379) at 15:44:47Z, the cart container failed at 15:44:50Z, the log instance cart/0.log of pod cart-74587775fc-dxrtf is absent from Loki, and all cart log lines after 15:45:08Z (later crash instances) lie outside the authorized window.

What deleted and replaced pod cart-74587775fc-t6vdk with cart-74587775fc-dxrtf at 15:44:46Z is unknown: Deployment cart stayed at revision 1 with an unchanged pod template, and no rollout, eviction, OOMKilled or unschedulable event for the cart pods was returned.

No cadvisor samples exist inside the authorized window for the new pod cart-74587775fc-dxrtf, so its memory/CPU usage and OOM counter at the time of the crashes could not be measured; kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason returned nothing for the cart pods.

Calico CRD-based network policies (GlobalNetworkPolicy/NetworkPolicy in crd.projectcalico.org) exist as CRDs but cannot be read with the available tools; the native NetworkPolicy query returned no objects, which only shows that query matched nothing. There is no change_history integration, so no record of who changed what.

No pre-incident baseline exists: the astronomy-shop pods were all created at 15:43:47Z and Prometheus/Jaeger data only starts around 15:44Z, so earlier error rates and latencies cannot be compared and no latency trend can be established.

The live in-memory flag state served by flagd could not be read; only the flagd-config ConfigMap (all defaultVariant 'off') was observable. Secrets could not be read, so any credential-dependent Valkey setting could not be verified.
next_steps: Read the current and previous cart container logs directly (pod cart-74587775fc-dxrtf) to capture the complete exception and any inner RedisConnectionException text for the latest crash instances.

Verify pod-to-Valkey connectivity and DNS from inside a cart pod (e.g., resolve valkey-cart and connect to 6379) and compare with the value the cart app actually uses, then compare the cart Deployment template with the reference chart.

Identify who deleted pod cart-74587775fc-t6vdk at 15:44:46Z (audit log / controller events) and check Calico CRD network policies and the live flagd flag state for cartFailure and failedReadinessProbe.
